transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I keep having these strange moments lately where things just feel off. My own house, or my office when I'm trying to work, just starts to feel completely unreal. It's hard to explain, but it's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there in my own body. It's been pretty unsettling, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.

When you feel like you're watching yourself from across the room, are you also aware that your surroundings—like your house or office—feel strange or unreal to you, or is it mainly just the feeling of being disconnected from your own body?

It's really both at the same time. Like I was just saying, the space around me—my house or my office—feels completely fake or unreal to me. And right along with that, I get that disconnected feeling where I feel like I'm watching myself from the outside instead of being in my body. So, yeah, it's not just one or the other... they definitely seem to happen together.

During these moments when you feel disconnected from your body and your surroundings feel unreal, do you know that it's not actually real—like, do you recognize it's happening but things just feel strange? Or do you sometimes question whether what you're experiencing might actually be real?

I know it's not actually real. Like, in my head, I know I'm sitting at my desk looking at tax forms, or standing in my own kitchen. I don't lose touch with reality or think I'm actually floating across the room. I know it's just a feeling... but it's a very strong, strange feeling. So, yeah, I'm aware that it's just my perception playing tricks on me, I guess. I never actually believe the world has turned fake.

When these episodes happen where you feel disconnected from your body and your surroundings feel unreal, do you notice them starting during times when you're feeling anxious or panicked? Or do they seem to come on their own without necessarily being triggered by anxiety?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. I mean, they just sort of happen. I haven't really paid attention to whether I was feeling anxious right before it starts or not. It's just... suddenly I feel that way, no matter what I'm doing.
Over the past few weeks or months, how often would you say these episodes happen? Are we talking about a few times a week, daily, or less frequently than that?

I'm honestly not too sure about the exact number of times. I haven't been keeping a tally or anything. It just feels like it happens when it happens, you know? I couldn't really say if it's daily or a few times a week. It's just something that comes up now and then.

Apart from these episodes where you feel disconnected from your body and surroundings, do you experience other symptoms like excessive worry, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, or a sense of impending doom on a regular basis?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed my heart racing or, you know, having trouble breathing or anything like that. And I wouldn't say I feel a sense of doom, either. It's really just... just that strange disconnected feeling I was telling you about. I don't really get those other physical panic feelings you mentioned.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed changes in your mood, such as feeling persistently sad, empty, or down? Or have you lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel sad or down, really. But... yeah, the interest part is definitely true. My wife tries to joke with me, or she asks about going fishing like we planned to do. And, you know, I know those things should feel good. I know I usually like them. But right now, it's like... it's like the part of me that enjoys them has just been switched off. I just don't feel much of anything toward them.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings—the disconnected feeling and the loss of interest in things you normally enjoy? Are we talking about days, weeks, or longer?

It's been about two weeks now. It all started right after... well, right after this incident at work where a client got really aggressive and actually threatened me in my office. So, yeah, since then, basically. Two weeks.

Since the incident at work two weeks ago, aside from feeling disconnected from your body and surroundings, have you been having intrusive memories of that aggressive client threatening you—like unwanted thoughts or images that pop into your head?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I don't get flashes of it or... or thoughts about it popping up when I don't want them to. It's really just the numbness and that weird disconnected feeling.

When you think about your day-to-day life right now, would you say the most bothersome part is that disconnected, unreal feeling you get? Or is it more that you feel emotionally numb and can't seem to feel much of anything, even for things that matter to you?

I guess... I guess they're both pretty bothersome, but if I had to pick one, it's the numbness. The disconnected feeling is weird, definitely, but not being able to feel anything for my wife or the things I usually care about... that's just hard to deal with. It just makes me feel totally empty.
Before the incident at work two weeks ago, were you experiencing this emotional numbness and disconnected feeling, or did those feelings only start after the threatening incident happened?
No, I wasn't feeling like this before. It definitely started right after the incident. Before that, everything was normal. I felt fine.
